claims.source: Based on this proteomic approach, the first 12 hr of illumination (T12) saw very few statistically significant changes in protein abundance (Figure 5—source data 1).
claims.evidence: Proteomic data analysis shows minimal changes in protein abundance during early de-etiolation.

claims.claim: Significant changes in protein abundance were observed only after 8 hr of illumination when considering a q-value <0.01 as a stringent threshold value.
claims.source: Considering a q-value <0.01 as a stringent threshold value, significant changes were observed only after 8 hr of illumination.
claims.evidence: Statistical analysis of proteomic data with specified threshold values.

claims.claim: At 8 hr, the abundance of cryptochrome 2 decreased and the abundance of three proteins (PsbS, Lhcb5, Lhcb6) belonging to chlorophyll a/b binding proteins increased.
claims.source: These changes correspond to the decreased abundance of only one protein (the photoreceptor cryptochrome 2, consistent with its photolabile property) and increased levels of only three proteins, which belonged to the chlorophyll a/b binding proteins category involved in photoprotection (AT1G44575 = PsbS; AT4G10340 = Lhcb5; AT1G15820 = Lhcb6; Chen et al., 2018; Li et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: Specific protein changes at 8 hr are identified from proteomic data and supported by literature citations.

claims.claim: A drastic change of proteome composition occurred by T24, with 402 proteins showing a significant increase in abundance with over twofold change (FC >2; q-value <0.01) compared with the etiolated stage.
claims.source: A drastic change of proteome composition occurred by T24, with 402 proteins showing a significant increase in abundance with over twofold change (FC >2; q-value <0.01) compared with the etiolated stage, and 107 proteins showing a significant decrease with over twofold change (FC <0.5; q-value <0.01).
claims.evidence: Statistical analysis of proteomic data at T24 shows significant proteome changes.

claims.claim: The 100 most-upregulated proteins at T24 comprised proteins related to photosynthesis, proteins constituting the core and antennae of photosystems, and proteins involved in carbon fixation.
claims.source: As expected, the 100 most-upregulated proteins comprised proteins related to photosynthesis, proteins constituting the core and antennae of photosystems, and proteins involved in carbon fixation (Figure 5—source data 1).
claims.evidence: Analysis of the most upregulated proteins from proteomic data.

claims.claim: 1112 proteins were assigned to plastids based on SUBA4 localization consensus.
claims.source: According to the SUBA4 localization consensus, 1112 proteins were assigned to plastids, which covers about a third of the total plastid proteome (Ferro et al., 2003; Hooper et al., 2017; Kleffmann et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Protein localization assignment is based on the SUBA4 database and supported by literature citations.

claims.claim: Hierarchical clustering of plastid-localized proteins revealed six main clusters with different accumulation patterns.
claims.source: Generation of a global heatmap for each of the 1112 potential plastidial proteins revealed different accumulation patterns (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1—source data 1). Hierarchical clustering showed a categorization into six main clusters.
claims.evidence: Hierarchical clustering analysis of proteomic data is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Cluster 1 contained proteins whose relative amounts decreased during de-etiolation.
claims.source: Cluster 1 (purple) contained proteins whose relative amounts decreased during de-etiolation.
claims.evidence: Cluster characteristics are described based on hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Clusters 2 and 6 displayed the largest amplitude of differential accumulation and were enriched in proteins related to the light reactions of photosynthesis.
claims.source: Proteins in clusters 2 and 6 displayed the largest amplitude of differential accumulation. Gene ontology (GO) analysis (Mi et al., 2019) indicated a statistically significant overrepresentation of proteins related to the light reactions of photosynthesis in clusters 2 and 6 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
claims.evidence: GO analysis of protein clusters is performed and results are reported with citation to the analysis method.

claims.claim: All photosynthesis-related proteins increased in abundance during de-etiolation.
claims.source: In agreement with that depicted in the global heatmap (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), all photosynthesis-related proteins increased in abundance during de-etiolation (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Photosynthesis-related protein accumulation patterns are shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Among eight detected chloroplast-localized proteins related to lipid biosynthesis, FAB1 and FAD7 levels increased only between T72 and T96.
claims.source: Among the eight detected proteins, two appeared differentially regulated; fatty acid binding protein 1 (FAB1) and fatty acid desaturase 7 (FAD7) levels increased only between 72 hr of illumination (T72) and T96, whereas the other proteins gradually accumulated over the course of de-etiolation (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: Lipid biosynthesis protein accumulation patterns are shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Illumination resulted in increased amounts of most proteins of the chlorophyll biosynthesis pathway, except PORA and to a lesser extent PORB, which decreased.
claims.source: In agreement, illumination resulted in increased amounts of most of all detected proteins of the chlorophyll biosynthesis pathway, except PORA and to a lesser extent PORB, which clearly decreased and were separated from other chlorophyll-related proteins (Figure 5C and Figure 5—source data 1).
claims.evidence: Chlorophyll biosynthesis protein accumulation patterns are shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The TOC receptors TOC120 and TOC132 were more abundant in etioplasts compared to fully-developed chloroplasts.
claims.source: Accordingly, the TOC receptors TOC120 and TOC132, which are important for the import of proteins in non-photosynthetic tissues, were more abundant in etioplasts compared to fully-developed chloroplasts (compare T0 and T96).
claims.evidence: Comparison of TOC receptor abundance between T0 and T96 from proteomic data.

claims.claim: The general import channel TOC75 (TOC75 III) maintained stable expression levels throughout de-etiolation.
claims.source: The general import channel TOC75 (TOC75 III) maintained stable expression levels throughout de-etiolation, reflecting its general role in protein import.
claims.evidence: TOC75 protein levels from proteomic data show stability across time points.

claims.claim: Immunoblot analysis revealed that the abundance of phyA dropped during the first 4 hr of light exposure.
claims.source: However, immunoblots revealed that the abundance of phyA dropped already during the first 4 hr of light exposure (Figure 6), as previously reported (e.g. Debrieux and Fankhauser, 2010).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6 show phyA decrease at early time points, supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: HY5 showed transient accumulation between 4 and 72 hr by immunoblot.
claims.source: The increase of HY5 peptide abundance was not significant by proteomics but we observed a transient accumulation of the protein between 4 and 72 hr by immunoblot (Figure 5—source data 1; Figure 6) consistent with the previously reported regulation of abundance during seedling development (Hardtke et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6 show HY5 accumulation pattern, supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: PsbA and PsbD proteins were detectable in seedlings at T4, gradually increasing thereafter.
claims.source: PsbA and PsbD (PSII reaction center core), PsbO (Oxygen Evolving Complex), and Lhcb2 (outer antenna complex) proteins were detectable in seedlings at T4, gradually increasing thereafter.
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show detection and accumulation of these proteins.

claims.claim: Accumulation of the PSI proteins PsaC and PsaD and the Cyt b6f complex protein PetC started at T8.
claims.source: Accumulation of the PSI proteins PsaC and PsaD and the Cyt b6f complex protein PetC started later; these proteins were detectable starting at T8 (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show detection of these proteins starting at T8.

claims.claim: AtpC (ATP synthase complex) was detectable in the etioplast.
claims.source: Interestingly, AtpC (ATP synthase complex) was detectable in the etioplast, as described previously (Plöscher et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show AtpC detection at T0, supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: ELIPs (Early Light Induced Protein) transiently accumulated upon the dark-to-light transition.
claims.source: As expected, ELIPs (Early Light Induced Protein) transiently accumulated upon the dark-to-light transition (Figure 6A; Kimura et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show ELIP accumulation pattern, supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: PORA accumulated in etiolated seedlings (T0) and then progressively disappeared upon light exposure.
claims.source: As in the proteome analysis, PORA accumulated in etiolated seedlings (T0) and then progressively disappeared upon light exposure.
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show PORA accumulation and decrease pattern.

claims.claim: PsbA levels were about twice that of PsaC at T96.
claims.source: In addition, the comparison of PsbA and PsaC (representative proteins of PSII and PSI, respectively) showed that PsbA levels were about twice that of PsaC at T96 (Figure 6B and C).
claims.evidence: Quantitative immunoblot data in Figure 6B and C show the relative abundance of PsbA and PsaC.

claims.claim: MGDG 18:3/16:3, MGDG 18:3/18:3, MGDG 18:3/16:1, DGDG 18:3/18:3, and DGDG 18:3/16:0 were the most abundant lipids detected at all time points.
claims.source: MGDG 18:3/16:3, MGDG 18:3/18:3, MGDG 18:3/16:1, DGDG 18:3/18:3, and DGDG 18:3/16:0 were the most abundant lipids detected at all time points.
claims.evidence: Lipidomic analysis identified and quantified these galactolipid species.

claims.claim: Clustering analysis identified two distinct kinetic patterns of galactolipid accumulation corresponding to the ER and PL pathways.
claims.source: Accumulation of all galactolipids increased upon de-etiolation; however, clustering analysis identified two distinct kinetic patterns. One group displayed a leap between T8 and T12, whereas the other group increased later during the de-etiolation period (Figure 7C). Interestingly, the two clusters separated the lipids according to the two pathways described for galactolipid synthesis, namely the ER and PL pathways (Figure 7A and B; Marechal et al., 1997; Ohlrogge and Browse, 1995).
claims.evidence: Clustering analysis of lipidomic data shown in Figure 7 reveals pathway-specific accumulation patterns, supported by literature citations.

claims.claim: During early stages of de-etiolation (T0–T24), there was incremental accumulation of MGDG and DGDG galactolipids derived from the ER pathway.
claims.source: During early stages of de-etiolation (T0–T24), we observed an incremental accumulation of MGDG and DGDG galactolipids derived from the ER pathway, whereas galactolipids from the PL pathway started to accumulate at T24 (Figure 7A and B).
claims.evidence: Lipidomic data in Figure 7A and B show pathway-specific accumulation patterns.

claims.claim: Galactolipids from the PL pathway started to accumulate at T24.
claims.source: During early stages of de-etiolation (T0–T24), we observed an incremental accumulation of MGDG and DGDG galactolipids derived from the ER pathway, whereas galactolipids from the PL pathway started to accumulate at T24 (Figure 7A and B).
claims.evidence: Lipidomic data in Figure 7A and B show PL pathway galactolipids accumulating starting at T24.

claims.claim: The MGDG/DGDG ratio decreased between T0 and T8, which was associated with the transition from PLB to thylakoid membrane.
claims.source: The MGDG/DGDG ratio decreased between T0 and T8. This was associated with the transition from PLB (cubic lipid phase) to thylakoid membrane (lamellar structure) (Bottier et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: MGDG/DGDG ratio calculation from lipidomic data in Figure 7D, with interpretation supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: The MGDG/DGDG ratio started to increase gradually at T8 and was constant by T72 and T96.
claims.source: The MGDG/DGDG ratio started to increase gradually at T8 and was constant by T72 and T96 (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: MGDG/DGDG ratio data shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: The chloroplast number per cell was constant from T4 (25 ± 8) to T24 (26 ± 6).
claims.source: The chloroplast number per cell was constant from T4 (25 ± 8) to T24 (26 ± 6); however, in parallel with cell expansion (Figure 8A and B), chloroplast number increased sharply (fourfold increase) between T24 (26 ± 6) and T96 (112 ± 29), indicating that two rounds of chloroplast division occurred during this time.
claims.evidence: Chloroplast number per cell was quantified from SBF-SEM data shown in Figure 8A.

claims.claim: Chloroplast number increased sharply (fourfold increase) between T24 (26 ± 6) and T96 (112 ± 29), indicating that two rounds of chloroplast division occurred during this time.
claims.source: The chloroplast number per cell was constant from T4 (25 ± 8) to T24 (26 ± 6); however, in parallel with cell expansion (Figure 8A and B), chloroplast number increased sharply (fourfold increase) between T24 (26 ± 6) and T96 (112 ± 29), indicating that two rounds of chloroplast division occurred during this time.
claims.evidence: Chloroplast number quantification from SBF-SEM data in Figure 8A, with inference about division rounds.

claims.claim: FtsZ1, FtsZ2-1, and FtsZ2-2 proteins were detectable during early time points of de-etiolation and accumulated significantly between T24 and T48.
claims.source: Immunoblot analysis of FILAMENTOUS TEMPERATURE-SENSITIVE FtsZ1, FtsZ2-1, and FtsZ2-2 proteins showed that these key components of the chloroplast division machinery were already present during the early time points of de-etiolation. We observed considerably increased accumulation of these proteins between T24 and T48, consistent with the idea that activation of chloroplast division takes place at T24, leading the proliferation of chloroplasts (Figure 8C).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 8C show FtsZ protein accumulation patterns.

claims.claim: ARC5 protein levels clearly increased during de-etiolation between T8 and T12.
claims.source: However, levels of ACCUMULATION AND REPLICATION OF CHLOROPLAST 5 (ARC5) protein, another key component of the chloroplast division machinery, clearly increased during de-etiolation between T8 and T12, presumably reflecting assembly of the chloroplast division machinery before its activation and the proliferation of chloroplasts (Figure 8D).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 8D show ARC5 protein accumulation pattern.

claims.claim: The average volume of dividing chloroplasts at T24 and T96 were consistently higher than the average volume of all chloroplasts.
claims.source: The average volume of dividing chloroplasts at T24 and T96 were consistently higher than the average volume of all chloroplasts (96 µm3 and 136 µm3 compared to 62 µm3 and 112 µm3, respectively) (Figure 4B, Figure 8E and Figure 8—source data 1) indicating that smaller chloroplasts are not dividing.
claims.evidence: Volume measurements of dividing chloroplasts from SBF-SEM data shown in Figure 8E.

claims.claim: Developing chloroplasts only divide once a certain chloroplast volume is reached.
claims.source: This indicates that developing chloroplasts only divide once a certain chloroplast volume is reached.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation that dividing chloroplasts have larger volumes than average.

claims.claim: The total thylakoid surface area present in seedling cotyledons at T96 was about 700 mm2.
claims.source: By T96, the latest time point of our analysis, the total surface area of thylakoids present in the seedling cotyledons was about 700 mm2 (see values in Table 1 for calculation), about 500-fold greater than the surface area of one cotyledon at this developmental stage.
claims.evidence: Calculation based on data in Table 1.

claims.claim: The total thylakoid surface area at T96 was about 500-fold greater than the surface area of one cotyledon at this developmental stage.
claims.source: By T96, the latest time point of our analysis, the total surface area of thylakoids present in the seedling cotyledons was about 700 mm2 (see values in Table 1 for calculation), about 500-fold greater than the surface area of one cotyledon at this developmental stage.
claims.evidence: Comparison calculation based on thylakoid and cotyledon surface area data.

claims.claim: The reorganization of pre-existing molecules rather than de novo synthesis is responsible for the major chloroplast ultrastructural changes that occur between T0 and T4.
claims.source: Therefore, our data suggest that the reorganization of pre-existing molecules rather than de novo synthesis is responsible for the major chloroplast ultrastructural changes that occur between T0 and T4.
claims.evidence: This interpretation is based on the observation of minimal protein and lipid changes between T0 and T4 despite major ultrastructural changes.

claims.claim: These results are consistent with other studies reporting only minor increases in protein accumulation and translation during initial chloroplast differentiation.
claims.source: These results are consistent with other studies reporting only minor increases in protein accumulation and translation during initial chloroplast differentiation (Dubreuil et al., 2018; Kleffmann et al., 2007; Reiland et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Comparison with literature findings supports the observation.

claims.claim: At T96 the abundance of 607 proteins (12% of the identified) was increased.
claims.source: At T96 the abundance of 607 proteins (12% of the identified) was increased which confirm the massive reorganization of the proteome following the reorganization of the transcriptome during photomorphogenesis (Ma et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: Proteomic data analysis at T96 with comparison to transcriptome studies cited.

claims.claim: Most photosynthesis-related proteins are globally coregulated.
claims.source: GO analysis combined with expression pattern–based hierarchical clustering highlighted that most photosynthesis-related proteins are globally coregulated (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, clusters 2 and 6) which correlates as well with the overall increase of their corresponding transcripts upon light exposure (Ma et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: GO analysis and clustering of proteomic data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1, with comparison to transcriptome studies cited.

claims.claim: PSI subunits were detected at later time points than PSII subunits, but thereafter PSI subunit accumulation was faster.
claims.source: However, targeted immunoblot analysis revealed different accumulation dynamics for specific photosystem subunits: PSI subunits were detected at later time points than PSII subunits, but thereafter PSI subunit accumulation was faster (Figure 6).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6 show differential accumulation dynamics of PSI and PSII subunits.

claims.claim: The kinetics of different photosynthetic parameters were consistent with the sequential activation of PSII and PSI.
claims.source: The kinetics of different photosynthetic parameters were consistent with the sequential activation of PSII and PSI, in particular photochemical quenching, which showed increased oxidation of the plastoquinone pool by T14 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Photosynthetic parameter measurements in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 support sequential activation.

claims.claim: Early accumulation of proteins such as Lhcb5, −6, and PSBS could be a way to quickly induce photoprotective mechanisms such as non-photochemical quenching to prevent PSII photodamage during initial photosynthetic machinery assembly.
claims.source: Early accumulation of proteins such as Lhcb5, −6, and PSBS could be a way to quickly induce photoprotective mechanisms such as non-photochemical quenching to prevent PSII photodamage during initial photosynthetic machinery assembly.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed early accumulation of these proteins and their known photoprotective functions.

claims.claim: Differences in PSI and PSII accumulation dynamics and activity have been consistently observed in other chloroplast development experimental systems.
claims.source: Differences in PSI and PSII accumulation dynamics and activity have been consistently observed in other chloroplast development experimental systems, including in Arabidopsis cell cultures, during germination and development of Arabidopsis seedlings in the light, and in tobacco leaves upon reillumination after dark adaptation (Armarego-Marriott et al., 2019; Dubreuil et al., 2018; Liang et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Comparison with multiple literature studies supports the observation.

claims.claim: The timing of PSII/PSI relative abundance do not match with their preferential localization in specific thylakoid membrane domains.
claims.source: Preferential localization of the PSI and PSII protein complexes in specific thylakoid membrane domains have been reported (lamellae and grana, respectively) (Wietrzynski et al., 2020). Therefore, the timing of PSII/PSI relative abundance do not match with their preferential localization.
claims.evidence: Comparison of observed accumulation timing with known localization patterns from literature.

claims.claim: Galactolipids constitute the bulk of the thylakoid membranes, but are mostly absent from other membrane systems under growth conditions where phosphorus nutrient is available.
claims.source: Galactolipids constitute the bulk of the thylakoid membranes, but are mostly absent from other membrane systems under growth conditions where phosphorus nutrient is available (Jouhet et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Statement about galactolipid distribution supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: MGDG and DGDG represent around 80% of the thylakoid membrane lipids.
claims.source: MGDG and DGDG represent around 80% of the thylakoid membrane lipids.
claims.evidence: Statement about galactolipid composition of thylakoid membranes.

claims.claim: ER-pathway galactolipids are predominant in the etioplast whereas PL-pathway galactolipids are predominant in the chloroplast.
claims.source: This illustrates the different galactolipid compositions of etioplasts and chloroplasts: ER-pathway galactolipids are predominant in the etioplast whereas PL-pathway galactolipids are predominant in the chloroplast.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the differential accumulation patterns of ER and PL pathway galactolipids.

claims.claim: The emergence of PTs relies on the existing lipids in the etioplast PLB.
claims.source: As no significant changes in lipid accumulation were observed by T4, it appears likely that the emergence of PTs relies on the existing lipids in the etioplast PLB, as suggested also by Armarego-Marriott et al., 2019.
claims.evidence: This interpretation is based on the lack of lipid changes at T4 and supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: Chloroplast development continued between T24 and T96, during which thylakoid membranes acquired grana stacks with more clearly defined organization.
claims.source: Chloroplast development continued between T24 and T96, during which thylakoid membranes acquired grana stacks with more clearly defined organization (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: TEM images in Figure 2 show continued structural development between T24 and T96.

claims.claim: Thylakoid surface increased by only 41% between T24 and T96.
claims.source: Thylakoid surface increased by only 41%; however, chloroplasts continued to enlarge at a rate comparable to previous de-etiolation stages (T0–T24).
claims.evidence: Calculation from thylakoid surface area data.

claims.claim: Chloroplast volume expansion between T24 and T96 may be caused by enlargement of extra-thylakoidal spaces occupied by emerging starch granules.
claims.source: This chloroplast volume expansion may be caused by enlargement of extra-thylakoidal spaces occupied by emerging starch granules.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observation of increased starch granules and chloroplast volume without proportional thylakoid surface increase.

claims.claim: Increases in lipids and proteins between T24 and T96 enable the expansion of already functional thylakoid membranes in preparation for chloroplast division.
claims.source: These results suggest that large amounts of lipids and proteins are necessary to build up the thylakoid membrane until T24, whereas increases in lipids and proteins between T24 and T96 enable the expansion of already functional thylakoid membranes in preparation for chloroplast division.
claims.evidence: This interpretation is based on the observed patterns of lipid/protein accumulation and chloroplast division.

claims.claim: Cell number was constant during cotyledon development and was estimated as 3000 mesophyll and palisade cells per seedling at T24 and T96.
claims.source: As reported previously (Pyke and Leech, 1994), cell number was constant during cotyledon development. We estimated this number as 3000 mesophyll and palisade cells per seedling at T24 and T96 (Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Cell number estimation based on volume calculations shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2, with support from literature citation.

claims.claim: The two approaches (mathematical model and morphometric measurements) showed very similar total thylakoid surface area per seedling at T4 and T24.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 9, the two approaches showed very similar total thylakoid surface area per seedling at T4 and T24 and differences in this parameter by T96.
claims.evidence: Comparison of model predictions with morphometric data shown in Figure 9.

claims.claim: The plateau phase suggested by the model is not validated and other components not included in the model probably contributed to the expansion of thylakoids at later time points of de-etiolation.
claims.source: This indicates that the plateau phase suggested by the model is not validated and that other components that were not included in the model probably contributed to the expansion of thylakoids at later time points of de-etiolation.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the discrepancy between model predictions and morphometric data at T96.

claims.claim: De-etiolation is divided into two phases: a 'Structure Establishment Phase' followed by a 'Chloroplast Proliferation Phase'.
claims.source: When considering chloroplast development, our study shows that de-etiolation is divided into two phases. We documented structural changes (disassembly of the PLB and the gradual formation of thylakoid lamellae) and initial increases of ER- and PL-pathway galactolipids and photosynthesis-related proteins (PSII, PSI, and Cyt b6f) during the 'Structure Establishment Phase', which was followed by increased chloroplast number in parallel with cell expansion in the 'Chloroplast Proliferation Phase'.
claims.evidence: This is a synthesis of the findings from structural, proteomic, and lipidomic analyses.

claims.claim: Compounds used to generate the mathematical model appear to contribute most to changes in thylakoid surface during early stages of de-etiolation (the structure establishment phase).
claims.source: This means that compounds used to generate the mathematical model appear to contribute most to changes in thylakoid surface during early stages of de-etiolation (the structure establishment phase).
claims.evidence: This interpretation is based on the good fit of the model to morphometric data at early time points.

claims.claim: During the later stages of de-etiolation (the chloroplast proliferation phase), the contribution of other compounds omitted in the model is required to build up thylakoid surface.
claims.source: By contrast, during the later stages of de-etiolation (the chloroplast proliferation phase), the contribution of other compounds omitted in our model is obviously required to build up thylakoid surface.
claims.evidence: This interpretation is based on the poor fit of the model to morphometric data at later time points.

claims.claim: FtsH proteases have a critical function during thylakoid biogenesis.
claims.source: Our proteomics data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Dataset 2) revealed some proteins that increased between T24 and T96, such as the FtsH protease (AT2G30950). FtsH proteases have a critical function during thylakoid biogenesis.
claims.evidence: Statement about FtsH function based on proteomic data and general knowledge.

claims.claim: In Arabidopsis, FtsH proteases constitute a hetero-hexameric complex of four FtsH subunits, which is integrated in the thylakoid membrane.
claims.source: In Arabidopsis, they constitute a hetero-hexameric complex of four FtsH subunits, which is integrated in the thylakoid membrane (Kato and Sakamoto, 2018).
claims.evidence: Statement about FtsH complex structure supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: Light triggers chloroplast differentiation whereby the etioplast transforms into a photosynthesizing chloroplast and the thylakoid rapidly emerges.
claims.source: Light triggers chloroplast differentiation whereby the etioplast transforms into a photosynthesizing chloroplast and the thylakoid rapidly emerges.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of the study's focus.

claims.claim: Using Serial Block Face Scanning Electron Microscopy (SBF-SEM), a series of chloroplast 3D reconstructions during differentiation were generated, revealing chloroplast number and volume and the extent of envelope and thylakoid membrane surfaces.
claims.source: Using Serial Block Face Scanning Electron Microscopy (SBF-SEM), we generated a series of chloroplast 3D reconstructions during differentiation, revealing chloroplast number and volume and the extent of envelope and thylakoid membrane surfaces.
claims.evidence: This describes the methodology and results of the SBF-SEM analysis.

claims.claim: Quantitative lipid and whole proteome data were used to complement the (ultra)structural data, providing a time-resolved, multi-dimensional description of chloroplast differentiation.
claims.source: Furthermore, we used quantitative lipid and whole proteome data to complement the (ultra)structural data, providing a time-resolved, multi-dimensional description of chloroplast differentiation.
claims.evidence: This describes the integrated approach of the study.

claims.claim: This study showed two distinct phases of chloroplast biogenesis: an initial photosynthesis-enabling 'Structure Establishment Phase' followed by a 'Chloroplast Proliferation Phase' during cell expansion.
claims.source: This showed two distinct phases of chloroplast biogenesis: an initial photosynthesis-enabling 'Structure Establishment Phase' followed by a 'Chloroplast Proliferation Phase' during cell expansion.
claims.evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract.

claims.claim: The data detail thylakoid membrane expansion during de-etiolation at the seedling level and the relative contribution and differential regulation of proteins and lipids at each developmental stage.
claims.source: Moreover, these data detail thylakoid membrane expansion during de-etiolation at the seedling level and the relative contribution and differential regulation of proteins and lipids at each developmental stage.
claims.evidence: This summarizes the comprehensive nature of the data collected.

claims.claim: A roadmap for chloroplast differentiation, a critical process for plant photoautotrophic growth and survival, was established.
claims.source: Altogether, we establish a roadmap for chloroplast differentiation, a critical process for plant photoautotrophic growth and survival.
claims.evidence: This states the overall contribution of the study.

claims.claim: Light is a crucial factor for chloroplast differentiation.
claims.source: Light is a crucial factor for chloroplast differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is a well-established fact stated in the introduction.

claims.claim: For seeds that germinate in the light, chloroplasts may differentiate directly from proplastids present in cotyledons.
claims.source: For seeds that germinate in the light, chloroplasts may differentiate directly from proplastids present in cotyledons.
claims.evidence: This describes an alternative developmental pathway.

claims.claim: Seeds most often germinate underneath soil, and seedling development typically begins in darkness and follows a skotomorphogenic program called etiolation.
claims.source: However, as seeds most often germinate underneath soil, seedling development typically begins in darkness and follows a skotomorphogenic program called etiolation, characterized by rapid hypocotyl elongation and etioplast development.
claims.evidence: This describes the typical developmental pathway studied in this work.

claims.claim: Etiolation is characterized by rapid hypocotyl elongation and etioplast development.
claims.source: However, as seeds most often germinate underneath soil, seedling development typically begins in darkness and follows a skotomorphogenic program called etiolation, characterized by rapid hypocotyl elongation and etioplast development.
claims.evidence: This describes characteristics of etiolation.

claims.claim: Light promotes seedling de-etiolation, which involves a series of morphological changes, such as cotyledon expansion, hypocotyl growth inhibition, and greening.
claims.source: Light promotes seedling de-etiolation, which involves a series of morphological changes, such as cotyledon expansion, hypocotyl growth inhibition, and greening, that accompanies the onset of photosynthesis in chloroplasts.
claims.evidence: This describes the de-etiolation process.

claims.claim: During de-etiolation, etioplast–chloroplast transition is rapidly triggered by light following seedling emergence at the soil surface.

results.result: Arabidopsis seedlings were stratified and exposed to continuous white light, leading to chlorophyll accumulation and establishment of functional photosynthetic machinery within 14 hours of illumination, as evidenced by maximum PSII quantum yield (Fv/Fm) reaching 0.8 at T14.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C5 describe the experimental setup and demonstrate functional photosynthesis establishment. The chlorophyll quantification (C3), photosynthetic efficiency measurements (C4), and multiple photosynthetic parameters (C5) provide converging evidence that photosynthetic machinery is operational by T14. The data are quantitative with appropriate replicates and error bars.

results.result: Major ultrastructural changes occur during the first 24 hours of de-etiolation, with etioplast PLBs (0.8-1 µm diameter) transforming into thylakoid lamellae by T4, followed by appearance of grana stacks (2-6 lamellae) and starch granules by T24, indicating photosynthetically functional chloroplasts.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C17 provide detailed TEM-based ultrastructural characterization with quantitative measurements of PLB dimensions, lamellae thickness, and grana organization. The presence of starch granules (C12) provides functional evidence supporting the structural observations. Measurements are consistent with literature values and include appropriate sample sizes (n=10).

results.result: Quantitative 3D analysis reveals that chloroplast volume increased 11-fold (9.4 to 112.14 µm³) and thylakoid surface area increased 30-fold (reaching 2086 µm²) from T4 to T96, with the most dramatic surface area expansion (22-fold) occurring between T4 and T24.
results.evaluation: Claims C18-C21 present quantitative morphometric data from SBF-SEM 3D reconstructions with appropriate error estimates. The measurements are internally consistent and the temporal dynamics clearly show two phases of development. The thylakoid/envelope surface ratio calculations (C21) provide additional validation of the structural changes.

results.result: Proteomic analysis of >5000 proteins reveals minimal changes during the first 12 hours of illumination, with only 4 proteins significantly changing by T8 (including photoprotective proteins PsbS, Lhcb5, Lhcb6), followed by drastic proteome reorganization at T24 with 402 proteins increasing and 107 decreasing (FC>2, q<0.01).
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C32 describe comprehensive proteomic analysis with appropriate statistical thresholds (q-value <0.01), sufficient replicates (n=3-4), and proper protein identification criteria (≥2 peptides, ≥1 unique). The hierarchical clustering (C29-C31) and GO analysis provide additional validation. The temporal dynamics are well-characterized across 8 time points.

results.result: Specific protein classes show distinct accumulation patterns during de-etiolation: lipid biosynthesis proteins FAB1 and FAD7 increase only between T72-T96, chlorophyll biosynthesis proteins increase except PORA/PORB which decrease, and TOC import receptors show differential regulation with TOC120/132 more abundant in etioplasts while TOC75 remains stable.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C36 describe specific protein dynamics from proteomic data. The observations are consistent with known biology (e.g., PORA photolability) and show appropriate temporal resolution. However, the functional interpretation of these patterns (C36) is somewhat inferential, though reasonable given the known roles of these proteins.

results.result: Immunoblot validation reveals differential accumulation dynamics of photosystem subunits: PSII proteins (PsbA, PsbD, PsbO, Lhcb2) are detectable at T4, while PSI proteins (PsaC, PsaD) and Cyt b6f (PetC) appear later at T8, with PsbA levels approximately twice that of PsaC at T96.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C44 provide immunoblot validation of proteomic findings with quantitative measurements using recombinant protein standards. The differential timing of PSI vs PSII accumulation is well-documented with multiple protein markers. The discrepancies with proteomics for low-abundance proteins (phyA, HY5) are acknowledged and explained by methodological differences.

results.result: Lipidomic analysis reveals two distinct kinetic patterns of galactolipid accumulation corresponding to ER and PL biosynthetic pathways: ER-pathway galactolipids accumulate incrementally from T0-T24, while PL-pathway galactolipids begin accumulating at T24. The MGDG/DGDG ratio decreases between T0-T8 (associated with PLB to thylakoid transition) then increases and stabilizes by T72.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C50 present quantitative lipidomic data with appropriate replicates (n=4) and clear temporal resolution. The clustering analysis (C46) successfully separates lipids by biosynthetic pathway, and the MGDG/DGDG ratio changes (C49-C50) are supported by literature citations linking lipid composition to membrane structure. The pathway-specific accumulation patterns are well-documented.

results.result: Chloroplast number per cell remains constant from T4 to T24 (25-26 chloroplasts) but increases fourfold to 112 by T96, indicating two rounds of division. Division machinery proteins (FtsZ1, FtsZ2-1, FtsZ2-2, ARC5) accumulate between T8-T48, and dividing chloroplasts have consistently larger volumes (96-136 µm³) than average, suggesting a minimum volume threshold for division.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C56 combine morphometric data from SBF-SEM (C51-C52, C55) with immunoblot analysis of division proteins (C53-C54). The inference of two division rounds (C52) is reasonable given the fourfold increase. The correlation between chloroplast volume and division capacity (C55-C56) is well-supported by quantitative measurements, though the mechanistic basis remains speculative.

results.result: The total thylakoid surface area in seedling cotyledons at T96 is approximately 700 mm², which is about 500-fold greater than the surface area of one cotyledon at this developmental stage.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C58 present calculations based on morphometric data from Table 1. The calculation methodology is described and the result emphasizes the remarkable expansion of photosynthetic membrane surface area. The comparison to cotyledon surface area provides biological context for the magnitude of thylakoid biogenesis.

results.result: The major ultrastructural changes between T0 and T4 occur through reorganization of pre-existing molecules rather than de novo synthesis, as evidenced by minimal protein and lipid changes during this period. This is consistent with literature reports and contrasts with the massive proteome reorganization (607 proteins increased) observed by T96.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C62 synthesize proteomic, lipidomic, and ultrastructural data to propose a mechanism for early chloroplast development. The interpretation (C59) is well-supported by the lack of molecular changes (C23-C24, C47) despite dramatic structural changes (C8). The comparison with literature (C60, C62) strengthens the conclusion, though the mechanism remains somewhat inferential.

results.result: PSI and PSII show differential accumulation dynamics with PSI subunits detected later than PSII but accumulating faster thereafter. This sequential activation is consistent with photosynthetic parameter kinetics and has been observed in other chloroplast development systems, though the timing does not match the preferential localization of these complexes in specific thylakoid domains.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C67 integrate immunoblot data (C63) with photosynthetic measurements (C64) and literature comparisons (C66). The observation is well-documented, though the mechanistic explanation remains speculative (C65). The apparent mismatch between accumulation timing and spatial localization (C67) is noted but not resolved, representing an interesting biological puzzle.

results.result: Galactolipids (MGDG and DGDG) constitute ~80% of thylakoid membrane lipids and are mostly absent from other membranes. ER-pathway galactolipids predominate in etioplasts while PL-pathway galactolipids predominate in chloroplasts, with the emergence of prothylakoids at T4 likely relying on existing etioplast PLB lipids due to lack of significant lipid accumulation changes.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C71 combine general knowledge about galactolipid distribution (C68-C69) with experimental findings (C70) and mechanistic interpretation (C71). The pathway-specific predominance (C70) is well-supported by the lipidomic data. The inference about PT emergence (C71) is reasonable given the lack of lipid changes at T4 and is supported by literature citation.

results.result: Between T24 and T96, chloroplasts continue developing with more defined grana organization, but thylakoid surface increases only 41% while chloroplast volume expands comparably to earlier stages. This volume expansion may be due to enlargement of extra-thylakoidal spaces occupied by starch granules, with lipid and protein increases enabling expansion of functional membranes in preparation for division.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C75 describe the later phase of chloroplast development with quantitative morphometric data (C72-C73). The hypothesis about starch granule contribution to volume expansion (C74) is reasonable but speculative. The interpretation linking molecular accumulation to division preparation (C75) is logical given the observed patterns but represents inference rather than direct demonstration.

results.result: Cell number remains constant at ~3000 mesophyll and palisade cells per seedling during cotyledon development. A mathematical model based on galactolipids and photosynthetic complexes shows similar thylakoid surface area to morphometric measurements at T4 and T24, but diverges at T96, indicating that other components not included in the model contribute to thylakoid expansion at later stages.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C78 present cell number estimates (C76) supported by literature and volume calculations, and compare model predictions with experimental data (C77-C78). The model validation at early time points and divergence at T96 is clearly documented in Figure 9. The conclusion that additional components are needed (C78) is well-supported by the data discrepancy.

results.result: De-etiolation divides into two distinct phases: a 'Structure Establishment Phase' (T0-T24) characterized by PLB disassembly, thylakoid formation, and initial accumulation of galactolipids and photosynthetic proteins, followed by a 'Chloroplast Proliferation Phase' (T24-T96) with increased chloroplast number during cell expansion. Model compounds contribute most during the structure establishment phase, while additional compounds are required during the proliferation phase.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C81 synthesize the major findings into a comprehensive model of chloroplast development. The two-phase model (C79) is well-supported by converging evidence from structural, proteomic, and lipidomic analyses. The differential contribution of model components across phases (C80-C81) is supported by the model-morphometry comparison. This represents the key conceptual advance of the study.

results.result: FtsH proteases, which form a hetero-hexameric complex integrated in the thylakoid membrane, have a critical function during thylakoid biogenesis and increase between T24 and T96, potentially contributing to the components missing from the mathematical model.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C83 identify FtsH as a candidate protein contributing to late-stage thylakoid expansion. The proteomic data support increased FtsH levels (C82), and the structural information (C83) is well-established in the literature. However, the functional role in explaining the model discrepancy remains speculative and would require additional experimental validation.

results.result: This integrated study using SBF-SEM 3D reconstruction, quantitative proteomics, and lipidomics establishes a comprehensive roadmap for chloroplast differentiation, revealing two distinct phases of biogenesis and detailing thylakoid membrane expansion with relative contributions of proteins and lipids at each developmental stage.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C89 summarize the study's approach and major findings as stated in the abstract. The multi-dimensional integration of structural, proteomic, and lipidomic data (C85-C86) is well-executed throughout the manuscript. The identification of two phases (C87) and comprehensive characterization (C88) are supported by the results. The claim of establishing a 'roadmap' (C89) is justified by the temporal resolution and quantitative nature of the data.

results.result: Background context establishes that light is crucial for chloroplast differentiation, which can occur directly from proplastids in light-germinated seeds or through etioplast-to-chloroplast transition during de-etiolation following dark germination. Thylakoid biogenesis, a hallmark of chloroplast differentiation, requires concerted synthesis and coordinated assembly of chlorophylls, lipids, and proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C97 provide well-established background knowledge about chloroplast development, supported by appropriate literature citations (C95, C97). These claims set the biological context for the study and are not novel findings but rather established facts that motivate the research.

results.result: Background on photosynthetic machinery describes the composition and function of the electron transport chain (PSII, Cyt b6f, PSI), electron carriers (plastoquinone, plastocyanin), ATP synthesis mechanism, complex subunit composition, protein synthesis requirements, and the TOC-TIC import machinery, establishing the molecular components examined in this study.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C109 provide comprehensive background on photosynthetic machinery and protein import, all well-supported by appropriate literature citations. These are established facts that provide context for interpreting the experimental results. The information is accurate and relevant to the study's focus on protein accumulation during chloroplast development.

results.result: Background on chloroplast membrane lipids establishes that chloroplast membranes are composed mostly of galactolipids (MGDG and DGDG) rather than phospholipids, synthesized via two pathways (ER and PL) distinguishable by fatty acid chain length at the sn2 position (18-carbon for ER, 16-carbon for PL), with galactolipids serving as integral photosystem components contributing to photochemistry and photoprotection.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C115 provide essential background on galactolipid biosynthesis and function, all supported by appropriate literature citations. This information is crucial for interpreting the lipidomic results and understanding the significance of pathway-specific galactolipid accumulation patterns observed in the study.

results.result: Background on electron microscopy techniques describes the evolution from conventional 2D EM to 3D electron tomography, which improved understanding of thylakoid organization and provided quantitative structural information, but is limited in observation volume. SBF-SEM overcomes this limitation by enabling reconstruction of much larger volumes through sequential imaging and cutting.
results.evaluation: Claims C116-C122 provide methodological background on electron microscopy techniques, supported by appropriate literature citations. This contextualizes the choice of SBF-SEM for this study and explains its advantages over electron tomography for whole-chloroplast 3D reconstruction. The technical limitations and capabilities are accurately described.

results.result: Background on thylakoid membrane composition establishes that biochemical fractionation has revealed differential lipid and protein compositions between grana (enriched in DGDG and PSII) and stroma lamellae (enriched in MGDG, Cyt b6f, and PSI), with changes in MGDG/DGDG ratio correlated with the transition from PLB/PT tubular structures to lamellar thylakoid membranes.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C126 provide important background on the relationship between membrane composition and structure, supported by multiple literature citations. This information is essential for interpreting the observed changes in lipid ratios and their correlation with structural transitions during chloroplast development.
